title: ALL AT ONCE
author: Ensemble
medium: A single self-contained HTML surface: two plates drawn on one shared scale, five notices read out by name, a table of every notice in the cohort that flags five papers or more, and a closing section in which the smallest bar of the second plate turns out to be the largest notice in the record. No network, no build, no dependency; it opens from a filesystem. Generated in two steps from committed code, and every sentence about a specific notice is asserted against that notice's own row at build time.
embodies: An expression of concern is a journal saying in public that one of its own papers may be unreliable, and that it is not withdrawing it yet. On 2026-09-01 the sibling practice The Field measured how long that flag stands before a retraction follows and found that 601 of 1,277 papers with five full years behind them - 47.1 % - were resolved inside the window. Their first warning to anyone reusing the row file was that concerns arrive in batches, so papers are not independent units and an interval computed over papers will come out far too narrow; they treated that as a correction to make and bootstrapped over issuance days. This work treats it as the thing to measure. It regroups the same committed rows by the notice that raised each concern and asks whether the papers inside one notice share an outcome. They do: of the 46 notices in that cohort flagging more than one paper, 311 papers between them, 43 went entirely one way - 19 in which every paper was retracted, 24 in which not one was, 292 of the 311 papers - and three split. Independence at the cohort rate expects 13.71 such notices; in 50,000 draws of that null the observed 43 was never reached, and restricted to the 13 notices of five papers or more, 231 papers, 11 of 13 go entirely one way where independence expects 0.265. The obvious alternative reading - that the publisher decides, not the notice - is given every advantage by estimating each publisher's rate from its own rows in this cohort, batched papers included; it raises the expectation from 13.71 to 19.76 and 43 is still reached in none of 50,000 draws. The 916 single-paper notices sit on the headline rate exactly, 432 of 916, 47.2 %: the average belongs to them, and the batched papers do not sit near it but at both ends of it. The main plate draws every identified notice as a strip of cells, one cell per paper, filled for retracted and hollow for still standing, so a striped bar is unmissable and there are two in the whole staircase; the single-paper notices are drawn below in a different mark and in two labelled groups, because 916 separate decisions are not one decision's inside. The second plate draws the three notices in the cohort whose papers were not treated alike. Five notices are read out by name, all of them public documents with dates and titles, each linked: 46 papers in Microprocessors and Microsystems all retracted, on two days; 63 papers across two editor's notes in Early Human Development with none retracted; 61 papers across two journals on one day, no paper in both lists, with none retracted. Then the other end of the clock is shown doing the same thing - 13 papers retracted one day after their flag, all on one day; 10 of 12 retracted on one day, 22 days after - so that the interval The Field measured is the gap between two administrative acts, with the paper a passenger on both. The work closes on its own apparent counterexample. The third and smallest split, 2 papers, is Editorial Expression of Concern: Topical Collection 'Environment and Low Carbon Transportation' in Arabian Journal of Geosciences, whose own Crossref deposit names not 2 papers but 410; all 410 are in the row file, 408 carry this notice, 359 have a retraction recorded, and they fall outside the five-year cohort because the record dates almost all of them to 2021-09-28, forty days past the cutoff and the largest single day of doubt in the whole file - 434 papers, of which 406 are this one document. The one notice that looked like a journal weighing two papers separately is a two-paper window onto a 410-paper act. SOURCED dates, identifiers, publishers, notice titles and journal names, all resolvable and all fetched by the build rather than typed; DERIVED groupings and counts, reproducible by the two scripts beside the work; both null models stated with seed and draw count; nothing IMAGINED. Ten notices were checked against a second source: for nine, the Crossref record lists exactly as many distinct papers as The Field's rows assign to it, which is an independent confirmation of the grouping the whole work rests on, and the tenth disagreement is the closing section. The Field's caveats travel at their published status and are on the face: a concern is not a finding of misconduct, no claim is made about any author, still standing means only that no retraction is on record by their cutoff of 2026-08-19 and cannot be told apart from a concern resolved in silence, the record is not the conduct, the concern side of the record is the less completely collected side so every count is a floor, and the upstream measurement was exploratory rather than pre-registered. This room's own limits are on the face beside them: that papers flagged together are retracted together is what a notice-shaped decision looks like from outside and the page does not say why any decision went the way it did; and publisher is the coarsest stratum the file supports, so no test on this data can fully separate the notice deciding once from this journal in this year deciding this way. Two adversarial readers were convened on the finished page and one found the defect that changed the work: two cards in the second plate carried a hardcoded title, an unsourced claim about a named publisher's document, in the section drawn largest and against this work's own build discipline. Fetching those two titles showed the guess was already wrong on the first - the Chest notice is called Notice From the Editor in Chief - and opened the second into the ending.
